name: HarborTech SafeScream SS-1 'Banshee'
description:
A keychain-sized personal alarm that emits a 142-decibel omnidirectional sonic burst when activated, producing a sound loud enough to cause immediate pain and disorientation at close range while alerting anyone within a 200-meter radius. The SS-1 activates via a pull-pin mechanism — yank the pin and the device screams until the pin is reinserted or the battery depletes, whichever comes first. The frequency is specifically calibrated to the human pain threshold: a warbling tone between 2,800 and 3,400 Hz that is physically impossible to ignore.

HarborTech designed the SS-1 after analyzing thousands of assault reports and finding that the single most effective deterrent was not pain or incapacitation but attention. Muggers, assailants, and opportunistic criminals in GLMZ rely on isolation and anonymity — the SS-1 eliminates both by making the attack the loudest thing happening within two city blocks.

The device costs Φ12 and runs on a standard coin cell battery that provides six minutes of continuous output. HarborTech distributes them through convenience stores, transit station kiosks, and community safety programs. In some Tier 1 neighborhoods, they are given away free by mutual aid organizations. The SS-1 is probably the single most widely carried self-defense device in GLMZ, surpassing even the SentryGuard PS-1 in sheer numbers.
specifications:
output: 142 dB at 30 cm
frequency: 2,800-3,400 Hz warbling
audible range: 200+ meters
battery life: 6 minutes continuous
weight: 22 g
dimensions: 4 cm x 2.5 cm x 1.5 cm
power source: CR2032 coin cell
cost: Φ12
tactical_use: Pull pin immediately when threatened. Do not wait to confirm danger. The SS-1's effectiveness comes from speed of deployment — the sound begins before the attacker can react. Hold the device away from your own ear if possible. The 142 dB output causes pain at one meter, making it a mild deterrent on its own, but its primary value is drawing attention to the situation. After activation, move toward populated areas while the sound draws witnesses.
cultural_context: The Banshee is GLMZ's great equalizer — no training required, no legal restrictions, and cheap enough that no one has an excuse not to carry one. Its distinctive warbling scream is universally recognized as a distress signal, and cultural norms in most tiers dictate that hearing one obligates bystanders to at least look and record. The sound has become so associated with danger that HarborTech had to issue guidance asking people not to use it for non-emergency purposes after a series of 'Banshee pranks' caused neighborhood-wide panic responses.
story_hooks: Someone has been placing modified SS-1 units in public spaces on dead-man timers — they activate at random, creating panic responses that serve as cover for coordinated thefts during the confusion.

A community organizer in Tier 1 has linked multiple Banshees together into a network that creates a rolling wall of sound — an improvised sonic barrier that has proven surprisingly effective at deterring organized criminal incursions into their block.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, oblong personal alarm resembling a small rounded rectangle—something between a lighter and a car key fob. Its diminutive size belies its acoustic violence. Designed to be instantly graspable and deployable, it sits in a palm like a worry stone but with purpose-built aggression.
physical_description.dimensions: 4 cm length × 2.5 cm width × 1.5 cm depth. Small enough to clip to a keychain or slip into a jacket pocket unnoticed.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 22 grams—nearly weightless in hand, giving it an almost disposable feel despite its serious function. The lightness makes it easy to carry constantly without fatigue or bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: High-impact ABS polymer composite shell housing an internal piezoelectric emitter assembly and coin-cell battery compartment.
physical_description.finish: Matte polymer surface with a slight grip-optimized texture. Impact-resistant but showing micro-scratches and scuff marks from daily keychain abrasion and pocket carry. Some units display wear patterns around the pull-pin mechanism from repeated practice activations.
physical_description.color_scheme: Safety-orange primary body with black accent bands framing the piezoelectric emitter port. The contrast serves dual function: visibility in dimly-lit urban environments and instant recognition of its purpose.
physical_description.grip_texture: Slightly textured ABS with micro-ribbing designed for secure grip even when wet or gloved. The pull-pin mechanism is knurled stainless steel, providing positive tactile feedback during draw.
distinctive_features: Protruding stainless-steel pull-pin with a textured ring head—visible and immediately graspable in high-stress situations
Circular recessed port on one end marking the piezoelectric emitter outlet
Small battery indicator LED (dim red when inactive, bright when recently deployed)
Micro-serrated edge around the emitter port to prevent accidental muffling if palm-cupped during activation
Molded safety warnings and frequency specifications in white text on the orange body
Slight manufacturing seam lines visible along the shell, typical of mass-production cost optimization
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HARBORTECH CONSUMER ELECTRONICS stamped in a recessed oval on the flat face. Serial number engraved beneath the battery access panel (rarely visible without disassembly). 'SS-1 BANSHEE' printed in block letters below the manufacturer name. Small compliance symbols indicating unrestricted sale in GLMZ.
physical_description.condition_typical: Most field units show moderate wear—the orange polymer faded to burnt amber from UV exposure and pocket heat. The pull-pin mechanism remains bright despite handling. Battery compartment may show corrosion patterns if left in humid environments. Units carried by Tier 2-3 residents often show nicks from contact with keys and loose change. Tier 1 devices are typically pristine.
